description:
`World::demand_function_scope` (src/compiler2/world.rs:2708) resolves a global
function by scanning every code. It collects `certain_homes` from
`CodeState::Indexed` codes, `pending` waits from `CodeState::Pending` codes, and
skips `CodeState::Scoped` entirely. It then returns:

    if certain_homes.len() > 1 { return Err(duplicate_function_diagnostic(...)); }
    if let Some(code_id) = certain_homes.into_iter().next() {
        return Ok(vec![FactKey::CodeScoped(code_id)]);
    }
    if let Some(code_id) = opaque_candidates.into_iter().next() { ... }
    return Ok(pending);

The `pending` vector is DROPPED on the single-certain-home path. If code A is
Indexed and Certain while code B (same global name+arity) is still Pending at
scan time, `certain_homes.len() == 1`, the scan resolves to A, and it never
re-runs -- once A reaches `Scoped` it is excluded from future scans. When B later
indexes, it looks like the sole home. The duplicate is never caught.

Deterministic (the scheduler is single-threaded) but dependent on `IndexCode`
completion order, so two textually identical duplicate programs can diagnose
differently based on parse cost or file size. Strictly a FALSE NEGATIVE -- it
never produces a wrong diagnosis.

The all-indexed case works and is covered:
src/compiler2/drive_test.rs:1169
`compiler2_duplicate_global_function_definition_diagnoses_instead_of_silently_picking_one`
asserts `resolve/duplicate-function` with message `` `foo/0` is already defined ``.

## Reachability, measured -- this is why it stays P4

Two same-file definitions are CLAUSES, not duplicates:

    $ printf 'fn foo(x), do: x + 1\nfn foo(x), do: x + 2\nfn main(), do: dbg(foo(1))\n' > dup.fz
    $ ./target/debug/fz2 interp dup.fz
    2

which matches Elixir. The defect needs two CodeIds defining the same global
name/arity, and the fz2 CLI submits exactly one user file. The runtime library
defines no global functions (`grep -c "^fn " src/modules/runtime_library/*.fz`
-> 0). So today the path is reachable only through the multi-`submit_code` API,
which is how the existing test reaches it.

## Fix shape

Make the scan wait until every same-name candidate code has settled
(Indexed-or-Scoped) before resolving -- i.e. do not drop `pending` when a certain
home exists -- or record the certain home as a fact re-checked at a barrier.

## Checks

- A test that submits `foo_first.fz`, drives until it is Scoped, then submits
  `foo_second.fz` defining the same `foo/0`, still reports
  `resolve/duplicate-function`.
- `compiler2_duplicate_global_function_definition_diagnoses_instead_of_silently_picking_one`
  stays green.

Old line reference world.rs:2339-2341 has drifted to ~2708-2741. Nothing else in
the old ticket was false.
title: Duplicate-global scan drops its Pending waits when one Certain home is found, so a late-indexing duplicate is never diagnosed
